claims.text: The FeNiCrMn HEA has a heterogeneous microstructure in its as-cast or annealed condition.
Instrumented nanoindentation can resolve spatially heterogeneous mechanical properties in FeNiCrMn HEA.
Local hardness varies spatially within the FeNiCrMn HEA.
Local elastic modulus varies spatially within the FeNiCrMn HEA.
Local hardness and elastic-modulus variations correlate with grain boundaries.
If second-phase regions are present, local hardness and elastic-modulus variations correlate with them.
Differences in local microstructural features cause differences in resistance to deformation.
Indents near grain boundaries exhibit different load-displacement responses from indents in more uniform regions.
Indents near second-phase particles exhibit different load-displacement responses from indents in more uniform regions.
A nanoindentation map will show statistically significant local variability in hardness.
A nanoindentation map will show statistically significant local variability in elastic modulus.
A homogeneous microstructure would yield relatively uniform mechanical-property measurements across the sample.
The proposed correlations can be detected only when the nanoindentation scale is sufficiently small to resolve the microstructural heterogeneity.
Macroscopic mechanical testing may produce results different from spatially resolved nanoindentation.
